name: VirtualActor
purpose: Location transparent single writer object addressed by type and id that holds private state and processes one message at a time on activation.
invariants: Only one invocation of a given ActorId runs at a time; concurrent calls MUST queue in arrival order.
Actor state NEVER escapes the actor instance; callers ALWAYS read it through invoke, never via direct store access.
Reminders MUST survive actor deactivation and restart; they SHALL fire after the configured period regardless of host.
Timers within an actor CANNOT outlive deactivation; reminders are the durable option.
Caller code MUST NOT depend on the physical host of an actor because placement can migrate on failover.
extension_contract: Implement new actor behaviors by subclassing a base actor type and registering it with the runtime; cross cutting concerns (tracing, policy) plug in as server side interceptors around invoke.

sources.locator: docs.dapr.io/developing-applications/building-blocks/actors/actors-overview/ Turn based access, Placement, Timers vs Reminders sections

why_essential: Per entity serialization (single writer) is a common need for accounts, devices and sessions; centralizing the primitive prevents ad hoc locks sprinkled across tools that drift under load.
alternatives_considered: Row level locks in the database which do not scale horizontally and couple correctness to a single DB
Rebuilding actor semantics with consumer groups which lacks reminders and state affinity
